title: Building a House from A to Z in 2027: 10 Steps for First-Time Owners
desc: The 2027 process for building a single-family house in 10 steps: land check, planning, design, permit, contractor, start, supervision, acceptance, as-built.
summary: A summary of 10 steps for building a single-family house, from preparing the land to taking over the house and completing as-built records, with links to detailed guides for each step.
body: Building a house is a major undertaking for any family, but many first-time owners do not know what to do first and what next. This article summarises the 10-step process for building a single-family house under current regulations; every step links to a detailed guide on the Quan Construction website.

Check the land papers. The land must have lawful papers and be used for the proper purpose; these papers are mandatory in a building permit dossier (Article 55 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP). Land without a land use right certificate (sổ đỏ) or that is agricultural land must be dealt with before you think about building.

Request planning information. Knowing the building line, density and permitted height in advance helps you design correctly from the start; see Requesting planning information before buying land or building a house.
Budget. Estimate construction, design, permit, tax and fee costs and a reserve for extras; see What costs a construction estimate includes.

Design the house. For a house under 3 floors, without a basement, with total floor area under 250 m² and under 12 m high, the owner may organise the design personally; a larger house must be designed by an organisation or individual with the relevant expertise and experience (Clause 2, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP). Details: Designing your own house: when must you hire a designer?.

Apply for a building permit unless the case is exempt (Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025). For the dossier, place of submission and time limit, see Procedure for a building permit for a single-family house.
3. Choosing a contractor and signing the contract

Choose a contractor and sign the contract. The investor is responsible for selecting the organisations and individuals it chooses to take part in construction activities (Clause 5, Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025). The contract should clearly state quantities, quality, schedule, price, payment and warranty; see House construction contracts: what to include.

Start of construction. Break ground only when the conditions in Article 48 of the Construction Law 2025 are met; see Conditions for starting construction of a house. The owner must put up a site sign at the entrance showing the owner's name, address and phone number, the name and scale of the work, the start date, the completion date and a perspective drawing (Point a, Clause 3, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).

Construction supervision. The owner organises construction and supervision and is responsible for the safety of the work, neighbouring works and the environment (Point b, Clause 3, Article 10). Items to supervise include construction methods, material quality, scaffolding, machinery and safety measures (Clause 4, Article 10). See also Is hiring a construction supervisor compulsory when building a house?.

Acceptance and taking over the house. A work may be put into use only after acceptance (Clause 2, Article 57 of the Construction Law 2025); on handover, the contractor must deliver the as-built drawings, the maintenance procedure and related documents (Clause 3, Article 58). See Acceptance of a house construction.

As-built completion (hoàn công), registering the house on the red book, and tracking the warranty. A single-family house carries a warranty of at least 24 months from completion of construction and acceptance for use (Clause 2, Article 129 of the Housing Law). See As-built completion and registering the house on the red book and Warranty for houses.
6. Three mistakes first-time owners often make
Finishing the design before asking about planning, then having to revise the drawings, losing time and money.
Signing a sketchy contract without drawings or an attached materials list, leading to disputes when extras arise.
Paying almost everything before acceptance and not retaining a warranty amount.
If you need a firm to accompany you from design and permitting through construction and as-built completion, contact Quan Construction for advice.

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The 2023 Housing Law is partly expired; some procedures also depend on the specific rules of the province where you build. Ask the commune- or ward-level People's Committee before preparing the dossier.
